title: 📢 Section 2 — Monologue Practice

sections.heading: What to expect
sections.body:
Section 2 is a single speaker talking about a general topic:
• A tour guide describing a venue
• A radio presenter announcing local events
• A manager explaining workplace facilities
• A student union representative giving an induction

There's NO conversation — just one voice. Questions include multiple choice, map labelling, form completion, and matching.

sections.heading: Key differences from Section 1
sections.body:
Section 1: Two speakers, everyday booking/enquiry
Section 2: One speaker, slightly more complex information

Section 2 often has TWO question types (e.g. multiple choice for Q11-15, then map for Q16-20). Read both sets during preparation time.

highlight: In Section 2, the speaker often gives a list of items with a description of each. Keep up by predicting when one item ends and the next begins.

question: A section 2 speaker says: "The sports centre has three main areas. First, the gym on the ground floor — that's open 6am to 10pm. Then the swimming pool, which is on the first floor and closes at 9pm. Finally, the courts..." What is the swimming pool's closing time?
explanation:
The speaker lists three items in order. For each, they give specific details:
• Gym: 6am to 10pm
• Swimming pool: closes at 9pm ← the answer
• Courts: details presumably follow

Listing structures are very common in Section 2. "First... Then... Finally..." signals three separate items — listen for the detail attached to each.

question: In the IELTS Listening test, Section 2 is DIFFERENT from Section 4 because:
options: Section 4 involves two speakers discussing an academic topic
Section 2 is about everyday topics; Section 4 is an academic lecture/talk
correct: Section 2 is about everyday topics; Section 4 is an academic lecture/talk
explanation:
Section 2: One speaker, everyday non-academic topic (tour, local radio, workplace induction)
Section 4: One speaker, academic lecture or talk on a university subject

Section 4 is typically the hardest — faster, more academic vocabulary, denser information.

sentence: In Section 2, the recording typically involves _______ speaker(s) talking about _______ topics.
explanation:
Section 2 = 1 speaker, everyday/social topics.
Section 4 = 1 speaker, academic topics.

Both are monologues but differ in register and difficulty. Knowing the format prevents surprises on test day.
